title: Shooting of ISIS-sympathizer Aaron Driver justified: Cops
article: An investigation into the shooting death of terrorist Aaron Driver answers none of the questions about police actions that put a cab driver in danger, the cabbie's lawyer said Wednesday.
"What stands out to me is what isn't in it. There doesn't seem to be an explanation of why my client was put in danger like that," Kevin Egan said.

In a release issued Wednesday, Strathroy-Caradoc police said a joint investigation with the OPP has been completed and determined the Aug. 10 shooting death of Driver, 24, in the driveway of a Strathroy home where he was living was legally justified.
The Ministry of the Attorney General reviewed the investigation and came to the same conclusion, the release said.
Police on the scene were faced with a suspected terrorist who had carried a backpack into the rear seat of a cab, and detonated an improvised explosive device (IED) inside, the release noted.

"Mr. Driver exited the vehicle and failed to comply with the police and their directions. Fearing for their safety and believing that Mr. Driver would detonate a second device the RCMP shot Mr. Driver, fatally wounding him," the statement said.

The statement says nothing about the man driving the cab, Terry Duffield. He was in the front seat of the cab when the device detonated. Duffield, who suffered minor injuries, scrambled out of the vehicle and was lying on the ground when police shot Driver.

Duffield says police had plenty of opportunity to warn his cab company about Driver or get him out of harm's way as he drove to the house and waited several minutes for the explosives-carrying terrorist to get into his cab.
Aware of the investigation's conclusions Tuesday before the official release, Duffield told The Free Press he has suffered anxiety and panic attacks since August and has not been able to work.
"They can finalize the justification of killing somebody, but wouldn't give me a straight answer on who decided to jeopardize my life," he said.
Police left the impression after the shooting that there would be a more wide-ranging investigation, Egan said.

"I thought it would be more far-reaching than to say it was OK to shoot him. I thought that there would be some investigation into the circumstances and why it got to that emergency situation," Egan said.

"It's interesting that it's Strathroy police and the OPP that did the investigation, when they were part of the (emergency) team. I'm not surprised that the police investigating themselves found that their actions were justified or that the attorney general did as well."
The OPP and Strathroy-Caradoc police have completed their investigation, Strathroy Const. Mark Thuss said.
The RCMP did not answer questions Wednesday about the possibility of other investigations.
An RCMP bomb analysis released recently shows the explosive was carrying 139 ball bearings and if it had detonated completely, would have caused a high risk of death to anyone within 1.5 metres.

"It still seems to be a salient point that they were aware Mr. Driver was going to go to a major centre to wreak some havoc and did nothing to warn the individuals who would reasonably be expected to transport him there," Egan said.
